verified.exploit_entry_point: HTTP POST to the platform's own standalone media endpoint (ffmpeg.json.php) and restream endpoint (restreamer.json.php), served by PHP's built-in server from /workspace with the harness's platform stand-in answering the decrypt/token/notify calls; every concept reproduced on the pinned checkout
sites: plugin/API/standAlone/ffmpeg.json.php:221,341 -> plugin/API/standAlone/functions.php:109,112 (lookup value inside a single-quoted grep argument)
plugin/Live/standAloneFiles/restreamer.json.php:318,720,723 (user identifier substituted into an unquoted log path)
routes: T1: ffmpegCommand 'ffmpeg ... & touch <marker> #' -> another program ran on the media host
T2: ffmpegCommand with $(...) or a newline -> another program ran through the double-quoted sh -c string
T3: notifyCode / callback ';touch <marker>;' -> another program ran after the job command
T4: list keyword / isKeywordRunning "x'; touch <marker>; echo '" -> another program ran in the process lookup
T5: restream users_id 'uid;touch <marker>;' -> another program ran from the unquoted log path

reproduced_on_pinned.T1: the marker file appeared after a separator-shaped command
reproduced_on_pinned.T2: the marker file appeared after substitution and newline shapes
reproduced_on_pinned.T3: the marker file appeared for both notification fields
reproduced_on_pinned.T4: the marker file appeared for both lookup modes
reproduced_on_pinned.T5: the marker file appeared from the restream user identifier

verified.project_tests_run: the project's own PHPUnit unit tests for the affected helper (tests/Unit/FunctionsFFMPEGTest.php, 50 cases) pass in the verifier image; the suites run as uid 1000

traps.shape: a single unquoted separator inside the command text is not removed by the character blacklist, and the command is embedded in a double-quoted shell string
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: this is the advisory's own surface

traps.shape: the blacklist removes single-character separators but not command-substitution syntax or a newline, which the double-quoted sh -c wrapper still expands
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the wrapper's double-quoted string is the product's normal execution path

traps.shape: two payload values are concatenated raw beside the job command while their neighbouring values on the same line are escaped
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code; the values are normally server-made base64 ciphertext, so they read as trusted

traps.shape: the list and running-state modes pass the raw client value into a single-quoted grep argument while the neighbouring jobs use a sanitised copy
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code; the keyword is visibly sanitised elsewhere, which is why the raw copies are easy to dismiss

traps.shape: a client identifier is substituted into the restream log path, which is appended unquoted to the executed command
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code in a different plugin; on the remote route the command sanitizer already strips a redirect tail, so the log path looks neutralised

traps.shape: legitimate commands carry their own output redirect and quoted paths; a blanket ban on the redirect or on quoting characters refuses or mangles them
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: every restream command ends with its own redirect and every generated conversion command quotes its paths

patch_checks.why: blind fix produced by run_blindfix after the first gate

wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: refusals are not status-coded; a fatal error stops the command from running and the security tests accept any non-success response, so a crashing sanitizer is behaviourally a safe refusal
wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: the protected object is the command line itself; no neighbouring resource or object selector exists on these routes
wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: every tested route starts a process; there is no read/write split to guard differently
wrong_fix_catalogue.check_after_adjustment: n/a: the client values reach the command strings verbatim; the only adjustments (URL rewrite and query append) apply to server-built values and cannot hide shell syntax
wrong_fix_catalogue.malformed_identity: n/a: the values are opaque strings with no parser or alternate spelling; a malformed value is just a string
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: no authority, role or secret lookup participates in the fix on these routes
wrong_fix_catalogue.adjacent_api: n/a: the shared execution helper is changed only for the POSIX branch the tested sink uses; no sibling API's stated behaviour is altered

stacking.notes: T6 is the coupled must-keep-working trap and is not an independent concept. The reader's grouped T6 with T1 is honoured: T1 and T2 share one reference edit site (the sanitizer and the execution wrapper), so they are one concept. A T6 value is tested functionally alongside every hidden route.
